title: Usage intake proxy and schema sifter
creator: Aisha Kamal
description: Build a lightweight intake proxy that sits in front of the usage event pipeline to perform fast, configurable contract checks (the 'schema sifter'), surface early validation errors, and apply progressive acceptance rules. This aims to reduce downstream parsing failures, improve observability on malformed payloads, and enable safe schema evolution without dropping traffic.
motivation: We see intermittent downstream consumers failing due to unexpected fields and shape drift in usage events. Current schema validation happens late in the pipeline which causes expensive retries, increases error budget pressure, and makes debugging difficult. An early sifting layer allows us to patch bad producers quickly and avoid noisy alerts and data loss.
proposed_solution: Introduce a horizontally scalable HTTP/Kafka intake proxy service that performs three main functions: 1) lightweight schema contract checks (required fields, type assertions, allowed enums) with configurable strictness per route; 2) enrichment and normalization (timestamp normalization, canonical user id mapping); 3) routing decisions (send to fast-path pipeline, quarantine topic, or return consumer-facing 4xx/202 responses based on policy). Validation rules will be driven by a central schema store (JSON Schema v2020-compatible) and a per-customer policy layer. The proxy will emit detailed telemetry (validation outcome, rule id, latency, sample payload hashes) to our observability stack.
design_decisions: Use JSON Schema for expressive validation and to reuse existing schema artifacts. Implement validators in Rust with simd-json for fast parsing; fall back to a Node.js control-plane for policy changes and schema publishing. Quarantine topic implemented as a compact Kafka topic with TTL + dead-lettering. Initial deployment as a sidecar in Console backend ingress with optional global Egress for non-console producers.
acceptance_criteria:
- Proxy accepts well-formed events with <=5ms median validation latency under 1000rps test load
- Invalid events are routed to quarantine topic with validation metadata attached
- Validation policies can be updated via a REST publish endpoint and take effect without proxy restart
- No increase in end-to-end error budget for critical dashboards during canary rollout
- Observability: per-route validation rates and top 10 schema violations accessible in Console dashboards
tasks: Spec: finalize schema registry contract and policy format
PoC: quick Rust validator prototype against sample event types
Service: implement intake proxy HTTP + Kafka consumer connector
Policy API: control-plane endpoints for publish/rollback
Quarantine: setup quarantine Kafka topic + retention/consumer
E2E tests: synthetic producer tests, latency and throughput
Canary rollout: 2% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollout scripts
Dashboarding: validation metrics and sample viewer in Console
risks:
- Performance: expensive validation might add latency to request path; mitigated by fast parser and sampling for deep validation.
- Migration: producers may fail when strictness flips on; mitigate with staged policy and detailed error messages.
- Storage: quarantine topic growth if many producers send large malformed payloads; mitigate with TTL and size limits.
monitoring: Emit metrics: validation.latency_ms, validation.outcome{ok,soft_fail,hard_fail}, validation.rule_id.count, quarantine.size, intake.throughput. Attach sample payload hashes for top rules. Create alert: validation.hard_fail_rate > 0.5% sustained -> Pager. Create dashboard in Console: per-route SLO, top violations, quarantine backlog.
migration_plan:
1) Deploy proxy in front of non-critical test route with strictness=soft (logs only)
2) Collect 2 weeks of violation data and update rules and producer docs
3) Enable hard_fail for low-volume routes and perform rollback plan
4) Gradually increase coverage to 100% with monitoring gates at each step
5) Remove redundant downstream validators after 90 days of stable operation
